title: Is sol so much worse than Astra?
author: Patient-Software-168
selftext:
Asking out of curiosity. 

  
I started my AI dev race a few days ago. Right before Astra came. 

  
I've started my little game project. I don't ask codex to write big stuff, I make a module at a time. 

  
Would Astra be better to start with already? Sol gets the job done, made the systems I wanted, I am just curious if Astra would bring me further. 

  
Asking chatgpt itself, it says I should build most of my game in sol as its cheaper and you can get alot more done, so it's not like chatgpt is biased towards making me want to use Astra.

comments.author: KHRZ
comments.body:
Hard to say for coding generally, but graphics got a lot better with Astra. (e.g. drawing vector graphics with code).

For a lot of coding tasks, latest models will be expensive overkill.

replies.author: Patient-Software-168
replies.body:
So for coding, sol. 
For graphics, Astra?

replies.author: wathappen
replies.body: Yes and not all graphics either. Small art isn’t very visible so you don’t gain much from using a more sophisticated model.

replies.author: TonyZwilde
replies.body: honestly, I think even Terra is enough for coding

replies.author: FailedGradAdmissions
replies.body: UI and Graphics Astra, anything else Sol is good enough, if you can pay for it have Astra make the plan and Sol implement

comments.author: daddytung
comments.body: Sol still gets the job done it’s not that is bad it’s that astra is just superior

comments.author: erratic_ostrich
comments.body:
Definitely no.  
If "sol gets the job done", then that's as good as it gets.  
Astra will just do the same but at a higher price.

Switch models only as needed, sol is probably the best choice for most task. Switch to astra only if you are working on something so complex that sol struggles with it.

And inversely, if something is too simple for sol, you may want to switch to luna or terra, which consume way less than sol.

And as a general rule, don't switch models between sessions because all previous context will be sent as input, wasting a lot of usage too.

comments.author: heavy-minium
comments.body:
My own observations: Astra needs little trial and error or rumination and is more precise, which helps a lot for many different use cases. In other words, it gets the job done with fewer tokens (which are more costly, of course) while still using proper precise language (no caveman speech).

For one, it can use the same context size more effectively, since it doesn't fill up with discarded/unnecessary info/insights as fast as other models. Retaining more useful context helps before compaction kicks in. This applies to images as well - they end up in the context just like text (remember, it's multimodal).

This allows for a more reliable feedback loop, which is perfect for "Here is a screenshot of the desired state, achieve that". Which is what the impressive showcases have been doing, basically.

The other thing is that being precise helps when handling things in other software via MCP. The model isn't constantly trying to backtrack to a prior state within the external software. Trial and error works well within a model's chain of thought, but much less when operating something via MCP tools.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
You won't notice a huge difference because you are restricting what you want to AI to do for you

That is one of reasons people should pay attention to those one-prompt posts. 

Obviously, you are new to this so you dont know but your "steps/iterations" are too small.

Building one small piece at a time can be done with even weaker models than sol and you may not notice a difference 

Its when you take bigger steps in each prompt, then the difference is clear

Personally for me, I am taking advantage of the fact that astra can handle visual targets

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body:
I mean... Small steps are good if you want to keep up with the work and really author it intentionally.  I don't necessarily think it's better to increase scope.  More a matter of preference.

I like my diffs to be maybe 500 lines.  Lines isn't a great measure, but the point is it's a reviewable, understandable piece of the system.  Just because Fable or Astra *could* write 25,000 lines and one shot a massive build doesn't mean that's the right choice.  That would take so much spec iteration up front to do intentionally without leaving design up to inference, and even then there would be gaps, no matter how smart the model is.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
its your time, your prompts, your project so it is entirely up to you

OP is saying he/she doesn't notice a difference and I am just explaining why.

I was never much of a perfectionist but I stopped caring about other aspects some time ago.

my priority is now just making a playable fun game and that's it.

honestly, if my game crashes after 6 hours or my game is a giant mess of spaghetti code, no players will notice because I can't even make a game interesting enough for them to notice

my point is that OP is cutting butter so using buffer knife is fine. Using a sharper blade wouldn't feel significantly different. the prompts aren't challenging enough to make a difference

comments.author: TonyDaDesigner
comments.body: no but astra blows it away for 3d modeling and animation

comments.author: CaptainAlexWest
comments.body: I use sol chat to plan and astra to cook. Astra is 25% better but it super cooks usage. It can do alot on low.

comments.author: Ill-Past4609
comments.body: Graphic wise yes, is it 2D or 3D?

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: Sol is dramatically worse at visual / spatial. But it's much worse from a token vs efficiency perspective with everything. It is by far the weakest price / performance ratio of Codex's models... aside from maybe Terra. Really if you want to save tokens, send things to Luna (varying levels, depending on your needs) which is the most efficient model Codex has. In fact Luna High is my main workhorse with Luna Max being the main subagent for tasks that need an extra oomph. However Astra handles all planning and spatial/visual concerns, especially when it comes to reviewing or assessing visual data or quality. Other models can't compare on that front.

comments.author: Significant_Swim8994
comments.body: And use both Codex and webchat, because if you pay they have each their own allotments of tokens.

comments.author: vlad_h
comments.body: No. I use sol for design and evaluation and have it write handoff instructions for Astra.

comments.author: because-potato
comments.body: I created an entire MMO with sol. Not sure what kind of graphics you are making, but I used pixel lab to make pixel sprites and they turned out phenomenal.
